article.title: Why a Stable Overall KPI Can Hide Major Customer Changes
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: An overall KPI can remain almost unchanged while important customer segments move sharply in opposite directions. Suppose a company reports a 10 percent conversion rate in both quarters. It may appear that nothing changed. But perhaps conversion among existing customers rose from 15 to 20 percent while conversion among new customers fell from 7 to 3 percent. Changes in segment size can make those movements cancel in the aggregate. This is why stable totals should not automatically be interpreted as stable behavior. Decomposition separates the overall metric into meaningful components. Analysts can compare segment-specific rates, population shares, product mix, regions, channels, tenure groups, or other dimensions related to the business mechanism. A weighted average is especially useful to remember: the total rate depends both on performance within each group and on how much weight each group has. Therefore an overall KPI can change because customer behavior changed, because the population mix changed, or both. Standardization can hold the mix constant to estimate what the total would look like under common weights. This helps distinguish composition effects from within-segment performance. Analysts should not create dozens of arbitrary segments until an interesting story appears. Segmentation should follow hypotheses about how the system works and should be stable enough to interpret. Visualizing contribution to total change can also help executives understand why a flat headline number deserves attention. The same principle applies beyond conversion: average spend, churn, defect rate, approval rate, and satisfaction can all hide offsetting movements. A useful report might say, “Overall conversion was unchanged, but this masks improvement among existing customers and deterioration among new customers.” That sentence turns a flat KPI into an actionable diagnosis. Stability at the top level is an observation, not proof that the underlying system is stable. Analysts should define the population, observation window, decision rule, and operational constraint before interpreting the metric. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文強調分析結果必須放回正確的 baseline、母體、segment、decision cost 與資料生成機制中理解。百分比、總體 KPI、model threshold 或部署後的新資料，都可能因分母、selection、population mix 或舊 policy 而改變含義。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：分析結果はbaseline、母集団、segment、decision cost、data generating mechanismと結び付けて解釈する必要がある。percentage、集計KPI、model threshold、deployment後のdataは、分母、selection、population mix、過去policyによって意味が変わり得る。
